name: Cohort Analysis Best Practices
description: This module captures the best practices for cohort analysis, distilled from common failure modes and what tends to hold up over time.
content:
This module captures the best practices for cohort analysis, distilled from common failure modes and what tends to hold up over time.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Before starting cohort analysis work, confirm the scope and constraints so the approach matches the actual requirement.
2. Re-check edge cases relevant to cohort analysis (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
3. Prefer the simplest cohort analysis approach that satisfies the requirement over a more general one that isn't needed yet.
4. Surface known limitations of a chosen cohort analysis approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.
5. Keep cohort analysis changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
6. State assumptions about cohort analysis explicitly before proceeding, rather than leaving them implicit.
7. When cohort analysis decisions are ambiguous, favor the option that is easiest to reverse or extend later.
8. Check that cohort analysis terminology is used consistently throughout, matching existing conventions in the surrounding context.
9. Measure before optimizing any cohort analysis bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.
10. Prefer explicit, readable cohort analysis solutions over clever ones that are hard to verify.
11. Validate cohort analysis outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.
12. When cohort analysis guidance conflicts with a specific user instruction, defer to the user's explicit instruction and note the conflict.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not skip documenting cohort analysis assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.
- Avoid introducing new cohort analysis abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.
- Do not apply generic cohort analysis advice without checking it fits the specific context at hand.
- Do not silently drop cohort analysis edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.
- Avoid mixing unrelated cohort analysis concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.

CLOSING NOTE
Revisit these cohort analysis guidelines if the task's constraints change significantly during the work.
